name: Joiakim
overview: Joiakim was a male priest from the tribe of Levi, identified specifically as the son of Jeshua and grandson of Jozadak. His role as a priest places him within the religious leadership of Israel during the post-exilic period. The biblical record concerning Joiakim is concise, focusing primarily on his priestly lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Joiakim means 'YHWH lifts up,' reflecting a theologically rich Hebrew name. This proper name, as recorded in Nehemiah 12:26, was not given directly by God but carries a meaning that acknowledges God's sustaining power.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Joiakim was the son of Jeshua, establishing a direct priestly lineage. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Joiakim's significance lies in his priestly heritage, serving as a link in the restoration of temple worship after the Babylonian exile. As a descendant of Jeshua and Jozadak, he represents the continuity of the Levitical priesthood entrusted with maintaining the covenantal worship of God. His mention in Nehemiah underscores the importance of priestly families in reestablishing Israel's religious life under God's guidance.
